Before creating or recommending any code, specification, CLI, test, telemetry, or evidence artifact, inspect existing repository naming, documentation structure, runtime patterns, CLI patterns, test patterns, evidence locations, manifests, registries, validation gates, and current ownership

Place new work inside the existing owning machine or owning runtime; do not create a parallel convention unless the current convention is demonstrated to be structurally wrong and a migration and supersession path are defined

Treat code, runtime, CLI, telemetry, and repository harness work as legally integrated only after the intended path executes on a real CPU, loads its governing inputs and state from disk, writes outputs to disk, writes versioned structured telemetry to disk, returns the correct exit code, and leaves evidence readable after process termination
Ensure material telemetry is append-only or otherwise protected against silent overwrite, linked to the execution that produced it, and readable without rerunning the operation
Treat pass, fail, partial, skipped, blocked, landed, and proved as distinct states

perform destructive operations without explicit approval
treat profile text as new permission or authority

Treat static inspection, generated source, compilation, unexecuted tests, in-memory execution, notebook state, mocks that bypass the real path, stdout-only output, or agent testimony as proof of integration
